A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoGHP research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoGHP benchmark results, architectural and hyperparameter ablations, learning curves and subgoal visualizations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional subgoal-noise, separate-actor and data-quality experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 15 changes the policy update from subtracting to adding the gradient of Jtotal, correcting its direction for the positive AWR objective. The architecture, objectives, generation procedure and teacher forcing remain unchanged. This establishes a pseudocode correction, not an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: v2 adds antmaze-medium-explore, antmaze-large-explore and scene-noisy evaluations, extending coverage to weakly goal-directed trajectories and noisier manipulation data within existing domains. Existing navigation, manipulation and pixel-based coverage remains; removing per-task tables does not establish removal of those evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the central comparison from six to eight baselines by adding OTA and SAW across all ten environments. HIQL also becomes an explicit comparator in the new subgoal-noise experiment. The original six baselines remain, including the unchanged pixel-based comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs inject Gaussian noise into predicted subgoals, apply the same perturbation to HIQL, and compare a separate low-level actor while retaining the subgoal generator. The original five-task evaluation protocol and Table 3 training settings remain unchanged. The Gaussian-noise magnitude is unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6-C.8 adds tests of subgoal-error robustness, the contribution of a unified actor, and sensitivity to dataset quality. Conversely, v1's advantage-temperature ablation and Transformer-versus-CoGHP learning curves disappear. The subgoal-count analysis moves into Section 5.4, with its cube-double curve revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across eight seeds for the main comparisons and most ablations, and four seeds for pixel-based results and loss-weight sensitivity. New experiments follow the existing eight-seed reporting practice; no changed uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains existing scores and adds OTA/SAW results. New findings include noisy antmaze-giant success of 73±2 for CoGHP versus 33±6 for HIQL, and scene-noisy success of 60±5 for CoGHP. Separate-actor results are added, the cube-double H=1 learning curve changes, and v1's temperature sweep, per-task tables and Transformer learning curves are removed.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the mathematical optimization direction from gradient descent to ascent on the positive advantage-weighted log-likelihood objective. This is a localized sign correction; the formal setup and Equations (1)-(14) remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified autoregressive subgoal/action generation, an MLP-Mixer backbone and strong long-horizon benchmark performance. Rephrasing CoT inspiration and replacing 'pioneer' with 'introduce' do not materially change these claims; Section 2 retains the first-use positioning.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets noise robustness through full-sequence conditioning and the separate-actor results as evidence for unified optimization. It also identifies dependence on trajectory structure under lower-quality data. The temperature-robustness discussion is removed, while the substantive limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-page access information. It removes Appendix A.2.2's blanket statement that navigation embeddings have dimension 32, which conflicted with the retained Table 3 specification of 128 for giant mazes. The hyperparameter table and Transformer implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to recent diffusion planners, action-autoregressive robotics, OTA and SAW, and presents CoGHP as complementary to these directions. Several embodied-reasoning citations are replaced. This updates the research context without fundamentally changing the retained relationship to HIQL or MLP-Mixer.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise the abstract, CoT motivation and comparison discussion. Subgoal-count analysis moves from Appendix C.2 to Section 5.4, and Transformer interpretation moves to Appendix A.4. Author notes, publication information, acknowledgements and cross-references are updated; most explanatory and methodological prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The evidence displays are substantially reorganized: Tables 1 and 9 gain comparison columns, new ablation and data-quality tables appear, and the temperature and four per-task tables disappear. The Transformer learning-curve figure is removed. Subgoal-count plots move into the main text with a corrected caption and revised cube-double panel; retained visualizations are relocated.

improvement.justification: The added recent baselines and separate-actor, noise and data-quality tests provide more direct support for the unified-policy design and clarify its limits. Correcting Algorithm 1 also improves technical consistency. These gains outweigh, but are tempered by, removal of per-task and sensitivity evidence and incomplete specification of the noise experiment, making the overall improvement limited.
